chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Hammad ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah the Exalted prohibited it upon my tongue, is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor to be believed when he narrates, nor interceded for when he intercedes, nor relied upon for an entrustment. So whoever trusts him with an entrustment and he consumes it or wastes it, it is not for the one who entrusted him, upon Allah Mighty and Majestic, that He rewards him or compensates him.'

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I intended to send goods to Yemen, so I went to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I intend to send so-and-so for the goods.' He said to me, 'Do you not know that he drinks wine?' I said, 'It has reached me from the believers that they say that.' He said to me, 'Believe them, for indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: He believes in Allah and believes in the believers.'

Then he said: 'If you send him and the goods perish or are lost, it is not for you upon Allah Mighty and Majestic that He rewards you or compensates you.' So I sent him and he wasted it, and I supplicated to Allah Mighty and Majestic that He reward me. He said: 'O my son, no, it is not for you upon Allah that He rewards you or compensates you.'

I said to him, 'And why is that?' He said to me, 'Indeed Allah Mighty and Majestic says: And do not give away your property to the foolish, which Allah has made for you a means of support. Do you know of any one more foolish than the wine drinker?'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The servant does not cease to be in a leeway from Allah Mighty and Majestic until he drinks wine. So when he drinks it, Allah Mighty and Majestic tears down his protective covering, and his guardian and his brother would be Iblis, may Allah curse him, and his hearing, and his vision, and his hand, and his foot, ushering him to every straying, and turning him away from every goodness.'

key_terms.يُزَوَّجَ: To be married to (in the context of a suitor)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal and spiritual consequences of drinking wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the drinker of khamr as 'safiha' (the foolish one), linking the physical act of drinking to a loss of legal credibility (shahada, marriage, trust) and spiritual alienation, where Iblis becomes his guardian. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the Quranic concept of 'sufaha' to justify trusting reports of drunkenness even if not definitively proven, emphasizing that the drinker's judgment is impaired to the point of spiritual folly. The narrative highlights the transition from being in Allah's 'fusha' (ease) to having one's 'sirbal' (garment of protection) torn away, marking a shift from divine favor to demonic guidance.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usma, from Hammad Bin Bashir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who drinks the wine after Allahazwj the High having Prohibited it upon mysaww tongue, so he is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor to be ratified when he narrates, nor interceded for when there is intercession, nor relied upon an entrustment. So the one who trusts him upon an entrustment, so he devours it or wastes it, so it is not for the one who entrusted him, upon Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic that Heazwj Rewards him or Compensates him’. And Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Iasws wanted to barter (trade) some goods to Yemen, so Iasws went to Abu Ja’farasws and said to himasws, ‘Iasws intend to send so and so for bartering goods’. So heasws said to me: ‘But, do youasws not know that he drinks the wine?’ So I said, ‘It has reached me from the Believers, they are saying that’. So heasws said to me: ‘Ratify them, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [9:61] he believes in Allah and has faith in the Believers’. Then heasws said: ‘If youasws were to send him for trading so if he destroys it or wasters it, so it would not be for youasws upon Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic that Heazwj Recompenses you nor Compensates upon youasws. So if youasws were to send him for barter and he wastes it, and youasws were to supplicate to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: ‘Recompense measws!’ Heasws said: ‘O myasws son! No, it is not for youasws upon Allahazwj that Heazwj Recompenses you, nor that Heazwj Compensates’. Heasws said: ‘Iasws said to himasws: ‘And why is that so?’ So heasws said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [4:5] And do not give away your property to the foolish which Allah has made for you a (means of) support. So, do youasws know of any one more foolish that the wine drinker?’ Heasws said: ‘Then heasws said: ‘The servant does not cease to be in a leeway from Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic until he drinks the wine. So when he drinks it, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Tears down his protective covering, and his guardian and his brother would be Ibleesla, may Allahazwj Curse himla, and be his hearing, and his vision, and his hands, and his feet, ushering him to every straying, and exchange him from every goodness’.
en.sarwar: 9. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Flammad ibn Bashir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one drinks wine after Allah, most High, has made it unlawful through my tongue, he then does not deserve to be married if he proposes marriage. He is not considered truthful if he speaks, his intercession is not accepted and he is not trusted about a trust. If one trusts him about a trust and he missappropriates it or loses it, then the one who has trusted him will have no reward with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, or replacement or compensation.’

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I once visited abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ‘I like to give a certain amount of asset to so and so to buy for me certain goods from Yemen.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you not know that he drinks wine?’ I replied, ‘I have heard from believing people who say so.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘You must believe them because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “. . . he believes in Allah and in the believing people.’”

He (the Imam) then said, ‘If you give a certain amount of assets and it is destroyed or lost, you will not have any reward or compensation for it with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious. For example, you give him your asset and he loses it. You then pray to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, for reward.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Never, my son, Allah will not reward you or compensate you for such loss.’

He (the Imam) has said, ‘I asked him (the Imam), ‘Why is it so?’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “Do not give to the dimwitted ones your assets which Allah has given you for your sustenance,” [4:5] do you see anyone more dimwitted than a wine drinker?’

He (the Imam) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘A servant has a chance before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, until he drinks wine. When he drinks wine Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, tears down his covering, then Satan, may Allah condemn him, becomes his guardian and brother, his ears, his eyes, his hands, his legs and he drives him to all misguidance and turns him away from all good things.”’
